According to Mark Gurman's latest Power On newsletter, Apple is preparing to include up to 1.5TB of memory in its upcoming M7 Ultra chip. This will finally allow Apple Silicon to match the maximum memory configuration offered by the 2019 top-of-the-line Intel Mac Pro.

The available memory capacity of Apple Silicon Macs has long been a limitation, primarily because Apple solders the memory onto the same package as the processor—while this design enables extremely high transfer speeds and is key to enabling unified memory, it also means memory capacity is constrained by the size of the chipset.

However, according to Mark Gurman, Apple appears to finally be preparing to close this gap. The company is developing an M7 Ultra chip configuration equipped with 1.5TB of memory:

He also noted that due to the current memory supply shortage, the final product may not come with 1.5TB of memory. Nevertheless, Apple's engineering design is indeed targeted at supporting that capacity.

Earlier this year, Apple discontinued the 512GB version of the Mac Studio equipped with the M3 Ultra chip, and subsequently also discontinued the 256GB version, leaving 96GB as the only memory option for the top-of-the-line Mac Studio. If purchasing the M4 Max model, the maximum configurable memory is 128GB.

Apple will launch its brand-new M5 Ultra chip later this year, equipped with up to 768GB of unified memory, setting a new record for Apple Silicon.

Based on Apple's current memory pricing (approximately $25 for each additional 1GB of memory), upgrading from the base 128GB configuration to 1.5TB could cost over $35,000.
